# Data Platform

## Definition

A Data Platform is the integrated set of technical capabilities — storage, processing, integration, metadata, security and operations — on which data is stored, transformed and served.

## Explanation

A platform is described first in terms of **capabilities** (technology-neutral), then realized by products. Typical capability groups: ingestion, storage, processing, serving, [[Metadata|metadata]] and catalog, [[Data Quality|quality]], security and access, orchestration, observability.

Platform styles include operational databases, data warehouses, data lakes, lakehouses and streaming platforms. [[Layered Data Refinement]] is a common structuring pattern; [[Governed Analytical Data Platform]] is the reference architecture in this knowledge base.

## Distinctions

- Platform vs [[Data Architecture]]: the platform is the realization substrate; architecture also covers meaning, models and governance.

## Examples

- A cloud lakehouse using [[Apache Iceberg]] tables, an orchestration service and a catalog.
